none.brief: On 9 December 2022 the Council adopted resolution 2664 by 14 votes to zero, with India abstaining. The Council kept its asset freezes in place while allowing eligible providers to meet basic human needs and deliver timely humanitarian assistance.

safeguards.brief: On 9 December 2022 the Council adopted resolution 2664 by 14 votes to zero, with India abstaining. The Council kept its asset freezes in place while allowing eligible providers to meet basic human needs and deliver timely humanitarian assistance. At adoption the ISIL and Al-Qaida regime's exemption applied for two years, with the Council intending to decide on an extension. The Council requested provider due diligence to limit prohibited benefits and gave the 1267 Committee a monitoring role.

india.brief: On 9 December 2022 the Council adopted resolution 2664 by 14 votes to zero, with India abstaining. The Council kept its asset freezes in place while allowing eligible providers to meet basic human needs and deliver timely humanitarian assistance. India raised diversion risks, sought proactive involvement of the 1267 Monitoring Team and robust reporting, and judged those concerns not fully addressed.
